title: Family & Pets (家庭与宠物)
description: Name your family members, count people and animals with the measure words 个 and 只, use 这 and 那 for this and that, say what you have with 有, and describe pets with simple adjectives.

notes.heading: 📌 Core Family Members
notes.body:
Chinese has different words for older and younger brothers and sisters — you must say which one you mean.

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 爸爸 | bàba | dad |
| 妈妈 | māma | mum |
| 哥哥 | gēge | older brother |
| 姐姐 | jiějie | older sister |
| 弟弟 | dìdi | younger brother |
| 妹妹 | mèimei | younger sister |
| 家 | jiā | family / home |
| 家人 | jiārén | family members |

💡 **Worked Example:** 我爱我的家人。Wǒ ài wǒ de jiārén. — I love my family. (爱 ài = to love; 我的 wǒ de = my)

📎 **Key Points:**
- The repeated-character words (爸爸, 妈妈) are said with the second character light and quick.
- 的 **de** shows possession: 我的妈妈 = my mum.

notes.heading: 👴 Grandparents: Two Sides of the Family
notes.body:
Chinese distinguishes grandparents on your **father's side** from those on your **mother's side**.

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 爷爷 | yéye | grandpa (father's father) |
| 奶奶 | nǎinai | grandma (father's mother) |
| 外公 | wàigōng | grandpa (mother's father) |
| 外婆 | wàipó | grandma (mother's mother) |

💡 **Worked Example:** 我的奶奶住在上海。Wǒ de nǎinai zhù zài Shànghǎi. — My grandma lives in Shanghai. (住 zhù = to live; 在 zài = in/at)

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** English 'grandma' covers both sides, but in Chinese 奶奶 and 外婆 are different people. Choose the right word for which grandmother you mean.

📎 **Key Point:** 外 **wài** literally means 'outside' — the mother's side was traditionally called the 'outside' family.

notes.heading: 🔢 Measure Word 个 — Counting People
notes.body:
In Chinese you cannot put a number directly before a noun. You need a **measure word** between them. The most common measure word is 个 **ge**, used for people and many general things.

**Pattern:** number + 个 + noun

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 一个人 | yí ge rén | one person |
| 三口人 | sān kǒu rén | three family members (口 is the formal measure word for family size) |
| 五个人 | wǔ ge rén | five people |
| 两个姐姐 | liǎng ge jiějie | two older sisters |

💡 **Worked Example:** 我家有四个人。Wǒ jiā yǒu sì ge rén. — There are four people in my family.

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** for 'two' before a measure word, use 两 **liǎng**, not 二 **èr**: 两个人 (two people), never 二个人.

📎 **Key Point:** the number 一 changes tone before 个: 一个人 is said **yí ge rén**.

notes.heading: 👉 This & That: 这 and 那
notes.body:
- **这 zhè** = this (near you)
- **那 nà** = that (far from you)

**Pattern:** 这/那 + 是 + noun

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 这是我爸爸。 | Zhè shì wǒ bàba. | This is my dad. |
| 那是我妹妹。 | Nà shì wǒ mèimei. | That is my younger sister. |
| 这是谁？ | Zhè shì shéi? | Who is this? |

💡 **Worked Example:** introducing a photo — 这是我的家人。Zhè shì wǒ de jiārén. (This is my family.)

🔑 **How it works:** before a noun you usually add the measure word: 这个 **zhège** (this one), 那个 **nàge** (that one): 这个女孩是我的姐姐。This girl is my older sister.

📎 **Key Point:** 谁 **shéi** means 'who' — it simply replaces the unknown person in the sentence, with no change in word order.

notes.heading: 🐶 Pets & the Measure Word 只
notes.body:
Animals are counted with the measure word 只 **zhī** (for most small animals and birds).

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 狗 | gǒu | dog |
| 猫 | māo | cat |
| 鸟 | niǎo | bird |
| 鱼 | yú | fish |
| 兔子 | tùzi | rabbit |
| 宠物 | chǒngwù | pet |

**Pattern:** number + 只 + animal

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 一只狗 yì zhī gǒu — one dog
- 两只猫 liǎng zhī māo — two cats
- 我家有三只鸟。Wǒ jiā yǒu sān zhī niǎo. — My family has three birds.

📎 **Key Points:**
- People → 个; most pets → 只.
- 一 changes tone before 只: 一只 is said **yì zhī**.

notes.heading: 🎁 Saying 'Have' — 有 and 没有
notes.body:
**有 yǒu** means 'to have' and also 'there is / there are'.

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 我有一个哥哥。 | Wǒ yǒu yí ge gēge. | I have an older brother. |
| 我家有一只猫。 | Wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī māo. | My family has a cat. |
| 我没有妹妹。 | Wǒ méiyǒu mèimei. | I don't have a younger sister. |
| 你有没有狗？ | Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu gǒu? | Do you have a dog? |

🔑 **How it works:** the negative of 有 is special — always **没有 méiyǒu**, never 不有. One common question pattern repeats the verb in positive and negative form: 有没有 (have or not have?).

💡 **Worked Example:**
A: 你有没有宠物？Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu chǒngwù? — Do you have a pet?
B: 有，我有一只狗。Yǒu, wǒ yǒu yì zhī gǒu. — Yes, I have a dog.

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** saying 不有 for 'don't have' — it must be 没有.

notes.heading: 🎨 Describing Pets: 大, 小, 可爱
notes.body:
Describe family and pets with simple adjectives. With adjectives, Chinese usually adds 很 **hěn** before the adjective instead of a verb 'to be'.

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 大 | dà | big |
| 小 | xiǎo | small |
| 可爱 | kě'ài | cute |
| 胖 | pàng | fat / chubby |
| 漂亮 | piàoliang | pretty |

**Pattern:** subject + 很 + adjective

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 我的狗很大。Wǒ de gǒu hěn dà. — My dog is (very) big.
- 这只猫很可爱。Zhè zhī māo hěn kě'ài. — This cat is very cute.
- 你的兔子很小。Nǐ de tùzi hěn xiǎo. — Your rabbit is small.

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** don't say 我的狗是大 — adjectives in Chinese do not need 是. Say 我的狗很大.

✅ **Check:** to put an adjective before a noun, add 的: 可爱的猫 (a cute cat), 大狗 (a big dog — 的 is often dropped after single-syllable adjectives).

flashcards.example: 这是我爸爸。Zhè shì wǒ bàba. (This is my dad.)
我妈妈很漂亮。Wǒ māma hěn piàoliang. (My mum is very pretty.)

flashcards.definition: Older brother. Younger brother is 弟弟 dìdi.
flashcards.example: 我有一个哥哥。Wǒ yǒu yí ge gēge. (I have an older brother.)

flashcards.definition: Older sister. Younger sister is 妹妹 mèimei.
flashcards.example: 那是我姐姐。Nà shì wǒ jiějie. (That is my older sister.)

flashcards.term: 爷爷 yéye / 奶奶 nǎinai
flashcards.definition: Grandpa / grandma on the father's side. On the mother's side: 外公 wàigōng / 外婆 wàipó.
flashcards.example: 我奶奶住在北京。Wǒ nǎinai zhù zài Běijīng. (My grandma lives in Beijing.)

flashcards.definition: The general measure word, used for people and many things: 三个人 (three people).
flashcards.example: 我家有五个人。Wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ ge rén. (There are five people in my family.)

flashcards.definition: The measure word for most small animals and birds: 一只猫 (one cat).
flashcards.example: 两只狗 liǎng zhī gǒu (two dogs)

flashcards.definition: This / that. Before a noun: 这个 (this one), 那个 (that one).
flashcards.example: 这是我的家人。Zhè shì wǒ de jiārén. (This is my family.)

flashcards.definition: To have; there is / there are. Negative: 没有 méiyǒu.
flashcards.example: 我有一只猫。Wǒ yǒu yì zhī māo. (I have a cat.)

flashcards.definition: Dog / cat — the two most common pets.
flashcards.example: 你的狗很大。Nǐ de gǒu hěn dà. (Your dog is very big.)
你有没有宠物？Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu chǒngwù? (Do you have a pet?)

flashcards.example: 这只兔子很可爱。Zhè zhī tùzi hěn kě'ài. (This rabbit is very cute.)

questions.explanation: 爸爸 bàba means dad. Like 妈妈 (mum), it is a repeated-character word said with a light second syllable.
姐姐 jiějie is the older sister; 妹妹 is the younger sister. Chinese always distinguishes older from younger siblings.
狗 gǒu means dog. A cat is 猫 māo, a bird is 鸟 niǎo, and a fish is 鱼 yú.
有 yǒu means 'to have' and 'there is/are', as in 我有一只猫 (I have a cat). Its negative is always 没有.

questions.stem: 可爱 (kě'ài) is used to describe something that is:
questions.explanation: 可爱 kě'ài means cute or lovely — perfect for describing pets: 这只猫很可爱 (this cat is very cute).

questions.stem: How do you say 'two older brothers' in Chinese?
choices: 二个哥哥 èr ge gēge
两个哥哥 liǎng ge gēge
两只哥哥 liǎng zhī gēge
二只哥哥 èr zhī gēge
questions.explanation: Before a measure word 'two' is 两 liǎng (not 二), and people take the measure word 个: 两个哥哥.

questions.stem: Which sentence says 'I don't have a younger sister'?
choices: 我不有妹妹。Wǒ bù yǒu mèimei.
我没妹妹有。Wǒ méi mèimei yǒu.
questions.explanation: The negative of 有 is always 没有 méiyǒu — never 不有. So 'I don't have a younger sister' is 我没有妹妹.

questions.stem: Your friend points at a photo next to her and says 这是我妈妈。(Zhè shì wǒ māma.) What does she mean?
questions.explanation: 这 zhè means 'this' (something near), so 这是我妈妈 is 'this is my mum'. 那 nà would mean 'that'.

questions.stem: Which measure word is correct in 我家有三___猫。(My family has three cats.)
questions.explanation: Cats and most small animals are counted with 只 zhī: 三只猫. 个 is the general measure word used for people.

questions.stem: 我家有五个人。(Wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ ge rén.) means:
choices: I have five people at school.
There are five people in my family.
questions.explanation: 我家 (my family/home) + 有 (there are) + 五个人 (five people) — the standard way to say how big your family is.

questions.stem: 奶奶 (nǎinai) is your grandmother on which side of the family?
choices: Either side — the word works for both
questions.explanation: 奶奶 is the father's mother. The mother's mother is 外婆 wàipó — Chinese uses different words for each side.

questions.stem: Choose the correct Chinese sentence for 'My dog is very big.'
choices: 我的狗是很大。Wǒ de gǒu shì hěn dà.
我的狗很大。Wǒ de gǒu hěn dà.
我的狗大很。Wǒ de gǒu dà hěn.
我很狗的大。Wǒ hěn gǒu de dà.
questions.explanation: With adjectives, Chinese uses subject + 很 + adjective and no 是: 我的狗很大. Adding 是 before an adjective is a classic learner mistake.

questions.stem: Someone asks 你有没有宠物？(Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu chǒngwù?) What are they asking?
choices: How many pets do you want?
questions.explanation: 有没有 (verb + 没 + verb) is a yes/no question pattern meaning 'have or not have' — so they are asking whether you have a pet.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says 'This rabbit is very cute'?
choices: 这个兔子很可爱。Zhège tùzi hěn kě'ài.
这只兔子很可爱。Zhè zhī tùzi hěn kě'ài.
这兔子是很可爱。Zhè tùzi shì hěn kě'ài.
兔子很这可爱。Tùzi hěn zhè kě'ài.
questions.explanation: Rabbits are animals, so they take the measure word 只: 这只兔子. The adjective 很可爱 follows with 很 and no 是.

questions.stem: 小明 says: 我家有四个人：爸爸、妈妈、哥哥和我。(Wǒ jiā yǒu sì ge rén: bàba, māma, gēge hé wǒ.) What do we know about him?
choices: He is the youngest child in his family.
He has an older brother and four pets.
There are four children in his family.
questions.explanation: He lists dad, mum, an older brother (哥哥) and himself — four people. Because his brother is a 哥哥 (older brother), Xiaoming must be the younger of the two children, so he is the youngest child in the family.
